purpose: Prototype v6p: does the rule stages' per-person reading also depend on the number of sentence starts per part? Asked by the pre-review of outline v12 for the Journal of Writing Research (round 6, R2 2 and R3 2: v6o split only the references, so its result that the shares go with smaller own distances may also bear on the summaries' negative results) and decided by the researcher (decision 29 of .steering/20261108-paper-a-jowr-reframe). Per dataset and baseline, the rule stages' persons are split by v6o's groups (n_s, and n_s_min beside it, with v6o's cuts), and per group the share of persons whose row exceeds their own parts is reported for each rule stage, beside R_loc and R_mean on the same persons. Per group, the gate rule (decision 25) says whether the stage is read: where R_loc reaches, as the procedure's reading; where only R_mean reaches, as a description; elsewhere not at all. The question read first: does 'I does not show LWP's inside' hold in the group with the most sentence starts per part?
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-11-09 after seeing the records and notes of v6k-v6o and the pre-review of outline v12 (round 6). The persons are v6m's (= v6n's = v6o's), whose v6m, v6n and v6o values have been seen, including v6o's shares of R_loc and R_mean per group of sentence starts. No share of a rule stage per group of sentence starts, and no per-group gate reading of a rule stage, has been computed or looked at. A first draft was sent to Codex (codex-consult, the conditions text and earlier aggregate results only, no data; .steering/20261109-v6p-rule-stages-by-sentence-count/codex-consult-output.md) and changed after its seven points (decision 1 of that folder): undecided and below are kept apart in the readings and predictions; the reading by group is fixed by a table over the rule cell's gate and the group's gate, and every group's state is counted; the ledger of what is written is stated per row and baseline with the reason; the guarantee is limited to linear derivation; the intervals are stated to be conditional; the predictions and the difference are stated on the interval; ties, empty groups, the classes at 0.60, the bootstrap and the keys are stated.
status: Description (status d) throughout: v6m's persons with v6m's, v6n's and v6o's values seen, and a split chosen after reviewers' questions. The readings below are fixed before any new value is seen; they are not a confirmation. No rule and no label. Applying the gate per group treats a group as a cell after the values of the cells were seen; it describes where the gate reaches by group and is not a new gate.

sources.v6n: works/conditions/prototype_v6n.json and results/prototype_v6n/record.json: the persons, rows, the rule stages' cells on their persons (rule_persons) and their keys; v6n's code is imported.
sources.v6o: works/conditions/prototype_v6o.json and results/prototype_v6o/record.json: the covariates n_s and n_s_min, the cuts, the groups, the written plan (small_derivable) and the groups' R_loc and R_mean cells on the persons with R; v6o's code is imported.

participants.persons: v6n's (v6m's draw, reused; v6n's checks of the id lists run).
participants.stage_persons: per dataset, baseline, row and stage, the persons of v6n's rule cell: the persons with the stage and R in the text and the row (v6n's rule_cell, extra R). They are a subset of v6o's cell persons (the persons with R; checked, the run stops otherwise), so every stage person has v6o's group. For U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I and U_med they are expected to be v6o's cell persons; for B_complete@2000 and Bsd_complete@2000 fewer (the run writes the persons per stage and row).

units_parts: as v6n: sentences (counting 'before'), parts odd/even and halves, one threshold 2000 ms.
stages: v6k's rule stages U@2000, B@2000, Bsd@2000, I, and v6m's stages beside them U_med, B_complete@2000, Bsd_complete@2000 (as in v6n's rule_persons).
rows: as v6o: v6n's eight dose rows (inside_25/50/75/100, cross_25/50/75/100) and v6k's three main rows (inside/before, shuffled/before, shuffled_in_halves/before). inside/before is the same row as inside_100.
fixed_by_construction: not split by group, written as fixed: U@2000, U_med and B@2000 under the inside rows (inside_25/50/75/100 and inside/before; each sentence keeps its multiset, v6n's INSIDE_FIXED), and B@2000 under shuffled_in_halves/before with halves (v6k's BY_CONSTRUCTION).

groups.how: v6o's: per dataset and baseline, the cuts c1, c2 of n_s (and of n_s_min) over v6o's cell persons, recomputed and checked equal to v6o's record (cuts and persons per group); each stage person keeps the group v6o gives that person. The cuts are not recomputed on the stage persons, so that a group means the same persons' range of sentence starts in v6o and v6p; for the stages with fewer persons the groups can be unequal (persons per group written).
groups.n_s_min: a sensitivity beside n_s, as in v6o; not a second test.
groups.matched_bands: not formed: v6o showed that KUPA essay and LWP barely overlap in n_s.
groups.edges: as v6o: ties at a cut go to the lower group; if c1 = c2 the mid group is empty, and then the family has a group under 5 persons and is withheld.

per_group.contributions: v6n's rule cell is computed on all its stage persons exactly as in v6n (checked against v6n's record: for the stage, R_loc and R_mean, persons, share_vs_own and its interval; paired_minus_R_loc's difference and interval). The per-person contributions (1, 1/2, 0; the full rule cell's scale over its stage persons) of the stage, of R_loc and of R_mean are then averaged within each group, so the groups' shares weighted by persons give the rule cell's share (checked to 1e-12 for each of the three).
per_group.stage: per group: the stage's share, its 95% percentile interval over 2000 bootstrap resamples of the group's persons, and its class against 0.60 as v6k (above if the lower end is above, below if the upper end is below, else undecided). Key numpy.random.default_rng([20261031, 99, dataset, task, stage index, row index, baseline, group, 0]) with v6n's stage and row indices (n6.STAGE of the stage's base name, n6.ROW_IX) and group 0 low, 1 mid, 2 high by n_s, 10, 11, 12 by n_s_min.
per_group.gate: per group: R_loc's and R_mean's share, interval and class on the group's stage persons. Where the stage persons are v6o's cell persons, the group's persons and contributions are v6o's, and the interval uses v6o's key for that reference, row and group, so the share, interval and class equal v6o's record (checked). Otherwise (fewer stage persons), the key is the stage's key with the last index 1 + the reference's stage index (R_loc 9, R_mean 13).
per_group.paired: per group: stage - R_loc and stage - R_mean, the mean difference of the per-person contributions on the group's persons with a 95% percentile interval over the stage's resamples of that group (the same resamples for both terms).
per_group.reading_by_group: per group, by the gate rule (decision 25) applied to the group, fixed by this table over R_loc's class in v6n's rule cell (all its persons) and R_loc's class in the group: (rule cell above, group above) 'gate'; (rule cell not above, group above) 'gate in group only'; (group not above, R_mean above in the group) 'R_mean only'; (neither above in the group) 'not read'. In 'gate' the stage's class is read as the procedure's reading on these persons; in 'gate in group only' it is read in the same way but only for that group and labelled apart, since the cell's gate does not reach; in 'R_mean only' it is a description; in 'not read' nothing is said of the stage in that group. Every written group's state is counted and written (not only the groups read through the gate), with the number of groups withheld.
per_group.difference: high - low of the stage's share, with a 95% percentile interval over the two groups' own resamples (independent groups), as v6o. Read as 'the high group's share exceeds the low group's' (interval above 0), not as a monotone rise; rising (low <= mid <= high of the point shares) is written beside.
per_group.rising: per cell, whether low <= mid <= high for the stage (only when all three groups are written).
per_group.classes: above if the interval's lower end is > 0.60, below if its upper end is < 0.60, else undecided (an end equal to 0.60 is undecided). 'undecided' and 'below' are kept apart in every count and reading: below says the share is under 0.60; undecided says neither.
per_group.interval_conditioning: every interval is over the group's persons with the full rule cell's scale, v6o's cuts, the per-person contributions and v6n's one random plan per person held fixed; it is not the uncertainty of rerunning the whole procedure on new persons, nor does it allow for the gate having been chosen on these persons.
per_group.share: the share is the mean of the per-person contributions with ties as 1/2 (v6b.one); 'reaches more often' below means a higher share in this sense.

written_plan.rule: per dataset, baseline, row and stage (not fixed by construction), the families of groups by n_s and then by n_s_min on the stage persons are added in that order; a family is withheld (persons per group only) if a group has fewer than 5 persons or if, with the sets already written, the sum over a set of 1-4 persons is a linear combination of the sums over written sets (v6o's small_derivable on atoms of membership over the dataset's count persons).
written_plan.already_written: for the row and baseline: the persons of v6n's count 1 cells (gate 0) of the stage, R_loc and R_mean; the stage persons of v6n's rule cell; v6o's written group families (v6o's cell persons by n_s and n_s_min). The sets are pooled over the stage, R_loc and R_mean as if they were one per-person quantity, which is conservative: R_loc on a stage's persons and R_loc on v6o's cell persons may differ in scale, but where the persons differ by 1-4 the difference of the sums could approximate those persons' contributions.
written_plan.withheld: if a family is withheld, nothing of its groups is written but the persons per group (no share, interval, class, reading, paired difference or difference).
written_plan.ledger: the ledger is per dataset, row and baseline, because the per-person quantity (whether the row's change exceeds the own distance) differs between rows; within a row and baseline it holds every set over which v6n, v6o and v6p write a share of the stage, R_loc or R_mean, pooled over these three as if one quantity. Paired differences and high - low are differences of the written group shares over the same persons and add no set. The check is run once more over the whole ledger of each row and baseline after every family is decided, before anything is written; a rerun (rerun_rule) writes the same sets.
written_plan.guarantee: the guarantee is that no sum over a set of 1-4 persons is a linear combination of the sums written. It does not cover inference from the values' constraints (contributions are 0, 1/2 or 1, so a share of 0 or 1 tells every member's contribution); such shares over 5 or more persons are written as in v6k-v6o.

primary: named before running, read first: I and Bsd@2000 at inside_75, inside_100 and cross_100, both sets and both baselines, by n_s (24 cells): per group the stage's share and class, the reading by group, stage - R_loc with its interval, and high - low. The other cells are listed as a table and not read one by one.

readings.a: In a group read through the gate ('gate' or 'gate in group only'): if the stage is above, on these persons the stage reaches the operation in that group; a 'does not show' over the rule cell is then an average over groups, and the paper's statement must name the persons and their sentence starts. If the stage is below, the summary's negative result holds on persons where the gate reaches in that group. If the stage is undecided, neither is read: the negative result is not reproduced there, and this is counted apart from below.
readings.b: In a group where only R_mean reaches: the stage's class is a description, as in v6n.
readings.c: In a group where neither reaches: nothing is said of the stage there. 'gate in group only' (e.g. a group where the gate reaches although the rule cell's gate does not) is read under (a) for that group only and counted apart from 'gate'.
readings.d: If the interval of high - low of the stage lies above 0: on these persons the high group's share of the stage exceeds the low group's; if it includes 0, a difference is not shown (not read as none: about 50-65 persons per group); if below 0, reported as it is. Neither is read as a mechanism or a monotone dependence; n_s is correlated with text length and other quantities not counted.
readings.e: stage - R_loc with its interval's upper end below 0 in a group read through the gate says that on these persons the stage reaches the operation less often than the reference (different numbers of features and scales; not read as 'the summary keeps less of the position').

checks.reuse: before any new quantity is reported, and stopping the run otherwise: v6n's persons and count persons; v6o's cuts and persons per group for both sets, baselines and covariates; for both sets, baselines, the eleven rows and the seven stages, v6n's rule cell (stage, R_loc and R_mean: persons, share_vs_own, its interval; paired_minus_R_loc: difference and interval); for the stages whose persons are v6o's cell persons, the groups' R_loc and R_mean share, interval and class equal v6o's record where v6o wrote them.
checks.groups: the stage persons are a subset of v6o's cell persons; the groups partition the stage persons; the groups' shares weighted by persons give the rule cell's share for the stage, R_loc and R_mean (1e-12); the parts' sentence starts are the same under every row (v6o's check).
checks.missing: as v6n: a summary over fewer than 5 values is not written; a non-finite value stops the run.

prediction: Claude's, written before running. P1: in LWP at inside_100, by n_s, under both baselines, the high group is 'gate' and I's class there is not above; reported with the class (below or undecided) apart. P2: in every group of the 24 primary cells that is 'gate' or 'gate in group only', the interval of stage - R_loc has its upper end below 0. P3: I's high - low (by n_s) has an interval including 0 in at least 8 of its 12 primary cells. P4: in KUPA essay under odd/even at inside_100, by n_s, the high group is 'gate in group only' and I's class there is not above (class reported). Not evaluable where a family is withheld. No new value has been seen.
main_cells: fixed before running, shown first: per set and baseline the stage persons per stage where they differ from v6o's cell persons; the 24 primary cells; then per stage and row a table of the groups' classes and readings; then over all written cells except inside/before the counts of groups by state ('gate', 'gate in group only', 'R_mean only', 'not read') and, within each state, of the stage's classes (above, undecided, below), with the number of families withheld.

record.public: results/prototype_v6p/record.json: counts and summaries over persons and the provenance; no press time, gap, key, text, per-person vector, value, n_s, change or id (ids only as the SHA-256 of their sorted list); a summary over fewer than 5 values is not written. The data are not redistributed.
record.provenance: git commit and dirty state of the conditions, code and lock; SHA-256 of the conditions, the earlier conditions and records, the code and the data; versions.

limits_written_before: The persons are v6m's with v6m's, v6n's and v6o's values seen, and the split was chosen after reviewers' questions about these results: nothing here is a confirmation. Three groups of about 50-65 persons; intervals are wide and a difference not shown is not an absence. n_s is one covariate among several correlated ones (text length, number of long gaps, typing speed) that are not counted. The groups share the full rule cell's scale, so a group's share is not what count 1 would give on that group alone. Applying the gate per group makes more, smaller cells after the cells' values were seen; a group read through the gate where the rule cell is not is a description. The cells are many and correlated (seven stages, eleven rows, two baselines, two sets, two covariates); no correction. The dose steps are four on one random plan per person (v6n). Only the 2 s threshold. A share shows sensitivity of a summary to a difference in press times; it says nothing about the cognitive meaning of a pause or the quality of a text. B_complete@2000 and Bsd_complete@2000 have fewer persons (persons without a complete burst are left out), so their groups are also a selection by that. The guarantee against deriving small sets is linear only (written_plan.guarantee). A continuous description of the stage's contributions against n_s is not counted (one more analysis chosen after the result).
rerun_rule: as v6k: if a defect of the code is found after the first run, the first record is kept unchanged, the fix and the reason are committed, and the rerun is reported separately beside the first.
generator: as v6k (checked by v6k's code against v6k's conditions).
implementation: the bootstrap interval is v6.ci (2.5th and 97.5th numpy percentiles, linear); the stage indices are v6n's STAGE of the base name (U 2, B 3, Bsd 4, I 5, Bsd_complete 7, B_complete 10, U_med 11; R_loc 8, R_mean 12), so no two stages share a key; inside/before is the same row as inside_100 and is written but left out of every count over cells (counts run over the ten other rows).
